boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Mary Washington
boards.description: Ten Fredericksburg food destinations with currently published evening hours; check the linked business page before heading out.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: 5325 Jefferson Davis Highway
cards.notes: Use the location page to confirm service and order options, then plan a breakfast, pickup, or delivery stop at any hour.
cards.short_summary: A nearly round-the-clock option for breakfast and diner food.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's lists this Fredericksburg location as open from 12 AM to 11:58 PM every day and describes it as serving breakfast 24/7.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily store hours of 12 AM–11:58 PM; pickup and delivery are offered.

cards.title: Hashtag Gyro And Subs
cards.subtitle: 11330 Patriot Highway
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s ordering options and posted hours, then use the carryout or delivery window for a late food run.
cards.short_summary: A casual gyro, sub, burger, and fried-chicken restaurant open through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Hashtag Gyro And Subs lists its Fredericksburg restaurant, carryout, and delivery hours as ending at midnight daily.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists restaurant, carryout, and delivery service through midnight every day.

cards.title: El Ultimo Trago
cards.subtitle: 9969 Patriot Highway
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location page to confirm the day’s closing time, then plan a dine-in or food-focused group meal.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant with a posted midnight Saturday closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: El Ultimo Trago lists Fredericksburg hours until 10 PM Sunday–Wednesday, 11 PM Thursday–Friday, and midnight Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site posts closing at 10 PM Sun–Wed, 11 PM Thu–Fri, and midnight Sat.

cards.title: Legends Grille
cards.subtitle: 10500 Spotsylvania Avenue
cards.notes: Check the day’s posted closing time and use the restaurant’s ordering link if a pickup plan works better than dining in.
cards.short_summary: A family-friendly American restaurant with late weekday and weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Legends Grille identifies itself as family-friendly and lists hours until 11 PM Monday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 11 AM–11 PM Mon–Thu, 11 AM–midnight Fri–Sat, and 11 AM–10 PM Sun.

cards.title: Chick-fil-A Fredericksburg
cards.subtitle: 4220 Plank Road
cards.notes: Confirm the current operating day first, then choose dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, or delivery before the 10 PM close.
cards.short_summary: A quick-service option with multiple official service modes through 10 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick-fil-A lists its 4220 Plank Road location’s dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, and delivery hours as 6 AM–10 PM Monday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists all service modes until 10 PM Mon–Sat; the restaurant is closed Sunday.

cards.title: Texas Roadhouse Fredericksburg
cards.subtitle: 3940 Plank Road, Suite A
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s waitlist or to-go option and confirm the day’s hours before making a later dinner plan.
cards.short_summary: A full-service dinner stop open until 11 PM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Roadhouse lists its Fredericksburg location open until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday, and until 10 PM Sunday–Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 11 PM closes Fri–Sat and 10 PM closes Sun–Thu.

cards.title: Castiglia's Italian Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 324 William Street
cards.notes: Check the dinner window before setting out, and use the restaurant’s stated take-out option if you need a shorter stop.
cards.short_summary: Downtown Italian dining with an 11 PM Friday and Saturday close.
cards.evidence_claim: Castiglia's lists hours until 10 PM Monday–Thursday and until 11 PM Friday and Saturday, with take-out available.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists closing at 10 PM Mon–Thu and 11 PM Fri–Sat; Sunday closes at 9 PM.

cards.title: Mi Rancho Mexican Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 3400 Plank Road
cards.notes: Confirm whether it is a Friday or Saturday, then choose dine-in, takeout, or the restaurant’s listed reservation option.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant open until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Mi Rancho lists its Fredericksburg location as open until 10 PM Sunday–Thursday and until 11 PM Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site posts 10:30 AM–10 PM Sun–Thu and 10:30 AM–11 PM Fri–Sat for the Fredericksburg location.

cards.title: Fahrenheit 132
cards.subtitle: 318 William Street
cards.notes: Reserve or confirm the evening schedule before leaving, especially for a Friday or Saturday dinner that runs to 11 PM.
cards.short_summary: A downtown restaurant with later Friday and Saturday dinner hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Fahrenheit 132 lists hours of 4–10 PM Sunday–Thursday and 4–11 PM Friday–Saturday at 318 William Street.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant page lists 4–11 PM Friday–Saturday and 4–10 PM Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Vocelli Pizza Fredericksburg
cards.subtitle: 7008 Salem Fields Boulevard
cards.notes: Check the official ordering page for the current day’s close, then place a pickup or delivery order before the listed 11 PM end time.
cards.short_summary: A pizza option with a published 11 PM closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Vocelli Pizza’s Fredericksburg site lists the 7008 Salem Fields Boulevard restaurant as open from 10 AM to 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official location site lists an 11 PM close; confirm the current day’s availability when ordering.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for studying, gathering, making, attending programs, and taking part in UMW community life.

cards.title: Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.subtitle: Ball Circle campus hub
cards.notes: Start on the second floor, then use the building’s lounges, reading nooks, meeting rooms, and dining level to fit the kind of break you need.
cards.short_summary: A four-story hub with shared spaces for academic and extracurricular time.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes the Cedric Rucker University Center as a campus center for extracurricular and academic pursuits, with study and social nooks, lounges, meeting rooms, and dining.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are listed as 7 a.m.–10 p.m. daily; some rooms are reservable or have specific access rules.

cards.title: Gourley Living Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.notes: Use the atrium seating for quiet reading or a low-key meetup before heading to another campus activity; keep the shared lounge comfortable for others.
cards.short_summary: Sofa-and-chair seating in the CRUC atrium overlooking Ball Circle.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies the Gourley Living Room as a second-floor CRUC space with chairs and sofas for quiet reading, gathering with friends, or hanging out.
cards.access_notes: Located in the CRUC; follow current building hours and any posted room-use guidance.

cards.title: South Living Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.notes: Choose this smaller atrium lounge when you want to read or catch up with a friend in a shared indoor space between campus commitments.
cards.short_summary: A smaller companion lounge in the University Center atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW lists the South Living Room with the Gourley Living Room as second-floor CRUC spaces with chairs and sofas for reading, gathering, and hanging out.
cards.access_notes: Located in the CRUC; use is subject to current building hours and event operations.

cards.title: Linden Terrace
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.notes: Take a seat on the balcony’s rocking chairs or at the indoor tables when the space is not booked, and leave it ready for the next group.
cards.short_summary: An indoor-outdoor terrace overlooking Ball Circle and its two linden trees.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says Linden Terrace has a balcony with rocking chairs overlooking Ball Circle, indoor soft furniture and tables, and is open for seating when not booked.
cards.access_notes: Open for seating when not booked for an event; located in the CRUC during its posted operating hours.

cards.title: Colonnade Room
cards.subtitle: Room 315, Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.notes: If your student organization needs a configurable meeting setting, coordinate a reservation and choose a layout that suits the group’s presentation or discussion.
cards.short_summary: The CRUC’s largest meeting room, with adjustable layouts.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies the Colonnade Room, Room 315, as the CRUC’s largest meeting room and notes that it has adjustable layouts.
cards.access_notes: A meeting space in the CRUC; reserve through the University’s current event-space process.

cards.title: UMW eSports Arena
cards.subtitle: Suite 306, Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.notes: Check with UMW esports or Athletics about current participation and event options, then use the arena as a starting point for a campus gaming community.
cards.short_summary: A campus arena supporting UMW’s student-shaped esports co-curricular experience.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW lists the eSports Arena in CRUC Suite 306 and says UMW esports offers a co-curricular experience shaped by students who want to grow and compete.
cards.access_notes: Located in CRUC Suite 306; confirm current program access, practice, and event arrangements with UMW Athletics.

cards.title: The Underground
cards.subtitle: Lee Hall
cards.notes: Check the Student Activities schedule for the week, then come for a club event, bingo, trivia, open mic, a small concert, or a study break.
cards.short_summary: Lee Hall’s evening programming space also set up for studying and eating.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says The Underground in Lee Hall is a place for students to study, eat, and enjoy campus entertainment, with weekly programming including bingo, concerts, open mics, and trivia.
cards.access_notes: During fall and spring semesters, listed hours are Sunday–Wednesday 5–11 p.m. and Thursday–Saturday 5 p.m.–1 a.m.; closed over summer.

cards.title: Hurley Convergence Center
cards.subtitle: Academic commons on the Fredericksburg campus
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from people or technology: reserve a room, ask a student consultant for help, or use the building’s study spaces.
cards.short_summary: A technology-and-learning commons with study rooms, production spaces, and peer support.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes the Hurley Convergence Center as an academic commons where students can reserve rooms for group study, use individual study spaces, obtain project help, and access media-production facilities.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are posted by day; UMW students, faculty, and staff can access the building 24/7 with an EagleOne swipe.

cards.title: Simpson Library Treehouses
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Simpson Library
cards.notes: For a distraction-light solo work session, head to the designated quiet third floor and choose a treehouse seat without treating it as group space.
cards.short_summary: Two-story study structures on Simpson Library’s quiet third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s Speaking and Writing Center identifies Simpson Library’s third floor as a designated quiet space with treehouses, and the university describes the floor as absolute quiet.
cards.access_notes: The third floor is designated quiet; check current Simpson Library hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Rock
cards.subtitle: Near the Campus Center
cards.notes: Look for the painted boulder near the Campus Center, photograph the current message, and follow campus guidance before adding any approved paint or announcement.
cards.short_summary: A named campus boulder used for student-painted messages.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s EagleSpeak glossary defines The Rock as a boulder near the Campus Center on which students may paint messages.
cards.access_notes: Near the Campus Center; consult current University guidance before painting or posting a message.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission options spanning UMW galleries and nearby National Park Service sites.

cards.title: See the exhibition at Ridderhof Martin Gallery
cards.subtitle: 1301 College Avenue · UMW campus
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then spend time with a few works and compare reactions. The gallery is next to Seacobeck Hall.
cards.short_summary: A free campus-gallery stop for looking closely at rotating art.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW Galleries states that admission is always free and lists Ridderhof Martin Gallery at 1301 College Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Open during exhibitions Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed during UMW holidays, breaks, and between exhibitions.

cards.title: Walk through duPont Gallery
cards.subtitle: 1913 College Avenue · UMW campus
cards.notes: Use the posted exhibition schedule before heading over, then make a slow circuit and discuss one piece that caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: A second free UMW gallery with its own exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW Galleries states that admission is always free and lists duPont Gallery at 1913 College Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Open during exhibitions Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed during UMW holidays, breaks, and between exhibitions.

cards.title: Take the Fredericksburg Battlefield tour
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Follow the park’s self-guided route at a comfortable pace, pausing at interpretive stops rather than trying to cover every landmark.
cards.short_summary: A National Park Service battlefield with self-guided exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists Fredericksburg Battlefield as part of Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park, which has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee; check current operating hours and conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Sunken Road tour
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg Battlefield · National Military Park
cards.notes: Start by the visitor center and use the NPS walking-tour guide for the half-mile route through the Sunken Road area and Marye’s Heights.
cards.short_summary: A guided-on-your-phone walk through a named battlefield landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS provides an onsite Sunken Road walking tour at Fredericksburg Battlefield; the encompassing National Military Park has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The Sunken Road is for pedestrian use; the park reports no entrance fee. Visit in daylight and follow posted conditions.

cards.title: Use the Chancellorsville driving tour
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Choose a few numbered stops from the park map and pair the drive with a short trail, keeping an eye on current facility hours.
cards.short_summary: A broad battlefield landscape with tour stops and trail options.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Chancellorsville Battlefield as one of the park’s sites; Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. Visitor-center and facility availability can vary, so consult current NPS hours.

cards.title: Explore Wilderness Battlefield stops
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Download the park map before leaving campus, then use the exhibit shelter and outdoor stops to shape a short, self-paced visit.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor battlefield destination managed by the National Park Service.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Wilderness Battlefield as one of the park’s battlefields; Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. Check current hours, weather, and trail conditions before heading out.

cards.title: Follow the Spotsylvania History Trail
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Use the NPS trail information to select a manageable section, then pause at earthworks and interpretive points along the route.
cards.short_summary: A battlefield with a documented history trail and open-air exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Spotsylvania Battlefield as part of the park; Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. The exhibit shelter is open sunrise to sunset; confirm current conditions for trails.

cards.title: Visit Chatham’s grounds and gardens
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Walk the grounds at an unhurried pace and use NPS interpretation to consider the site’s plantation, hospital, and headquarters history.
cards.short_summary: A historic NPS site overlooking Fredericksburg.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Chatham as a site within Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park, which has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. Chatham’s grounds are generally open sunrise to sunset; verify current building access separately.

cards.title: Walk the Ellwood Manor grounds
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Plan this as an outdoor history stop: read the site context first, then give yourself time to take in the manor and surrounding landscape.
cards.short_summary: A named historic site within the no-fee National Military Park.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Ellwood as a site of Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park, which has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. Interior access is seasonal and may be closed; consult NPS operating-hours information.

cards.title: See the Jackson Death Site grounds
cards.subtitle: Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.notes: Treat this as a brief, reflective stop and read the NPS context on the former Fairfield Plantation before or during your visit.
cards.short_summary: A historic NPS site with daily sunrise-to-sunset grounds access.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies the Jackson Death Site within Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park, which has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: The park reports no entrance fee. Grounds are open daily sunrise to sunset; the building is open seasonally.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments across Simpson Library, the Hurley Convergence Center, and the Cedric Rucker University Center.

cards.title: Simpson Library Individual Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Simpson Library — all three floors
cards.notes: Choose an individual study area on any library floor, then use campus wireless and nearby printing or copying when your work calls for it.
cards.short_summary: Flexible solo-study seating throughout Simpson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW states that Simpson Library has individual study areas on all three floors, campus wireless, printing, and copying.
cards.source_title: Simpson Library | University of Mary Washington Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located in Simpson Library; consult current library building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Simpson Library Group Work Tables
cards.subtitle: Simpson Library
cards.notes: Bring a project group to the library’s group-work tables and keep the session focused on shared notes, screens, and problem-solving.
cards.short_summary: Table seating designed for collaborative library work.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW lists tables for group work among Simpson Library’s study spaces.
cards.source_title: Simpson Library | University of Mary Washington Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located in Simpson Library; consult current library building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Simpson Library Reservable Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Simpson Library
cards.notes: Reserve a library study room for a defined group session, especially when you need a contained setting for discussion or shared coursework.
cards.short_summary: Bookable rooms for focused group sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies reservable study rooms as part of Simpson Library’s group and individual study spaces.
cards.source_title: Simpson Library | University of Mary Washington Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required for planned use; check the library’s current room-booking system and eligibility rules.

cards.title: Simpson Library Sunrooms
cards.subtitle: Simpson Library
cards.notes: Settle into a sunroom’s soft seating for reading, outlining, or laptop work when a conventional desk is not what you need.
cards.short_summary: Soft-seating study spaces inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Simpson Library’s sunrooms as cozy spaces with soft seating.
cards.source_title: Simpson Library | University of Mary Washington Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located in Simpson Library; consult current library building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Simpson Library Treehouses
cards.subtitle: Simpson Library — third floor
cards.notes: Use a double-decker treehouse carrel for a solo reading or writing block; bring only the materials you need to keep the setup simple.
cards.short_summary: Double-decker study carrels on the third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies the treehouses as double-decker study carrels located on Simpson Library’s third floor.
cards.source_title: Simpson Library | University of Mary Washington Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Third-floor location in Simpson Library; consult current library building hours before visiting.

cards.title: HCC Computer Workstations
cards.subtitle: Hurley Convergence Center
cards.notes: Use an HCC computer workstation when your assignment needs campus hardware or software instead of a personal-device-only setup.
cards.short_summary: Campus computer access for technology-dependent work.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s Off-Campus Student Services lists computers at the Hurley Convergence Center as a study resource.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Student Services | University of Mary Washington
cards.access_notes: Located in the Hurley Convergence Center; workstation availability and building access may vary.

cards.title: HCC Worktables
cards.subtitle: Hurley Convergence Center
cards.notes: Use an HCC worktable for spreading out course materials or collaborating face-to-face; pack up promptly when you finish.
cards.short_summary: Shared table workspace in the Hurley Convergence Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s Off-Campus Student Services lists worktables at the Hurley Convergence Center as a study resource.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Student Services | University of Mary Washington
cards.access_notes: Located in the Hurley Convergence Center; table availability and building access may vary.

cards.title: HCC Private Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hurley Convergence Center
cards.notes: Plan a private-room session for concentrated work or a small collaboration, and use the linked room-reservation process before relying on one.
cards.short_summary: Private HCC rooms with a reservation path.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s Off-Campus Student Services lists private rooms at the Hurley Convergence Center and links to room reservations.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Student Services | University of Mary Washington
cards.access_notes: Private rooms require checking the current HCC reservation process; availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: CRUC Third-Floor Reading Nooks
cards.subtitle: Cedric Rucker University Center — third floor
cards.notes: Take a small reading nook for independent coursework or a quiet check-in with classmates, keeping the compact seating arrangement in mind.
cards.short_summary: Small chair-and-table nooks on the CRUC’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says the CRUC third floor has several reading nooks with chairs and tables or groups of lounge chairs for studying.
cards.source_title: About the Cedric Rucker University Center | University of Mary Washington
cards.access_notes: CRUC academic-year building hours are listed as daily 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; hours change during breaks.

cards.title: Linden Terrace
cards.subtitle: Cedric Rucker University Center — fourth floor
cards.notes: Use Linden Terrace’s indoor soft furniture, tables, or rocking-chair balcony for coursework when the space is not booked for an event.
cards.short_summary: Indoor and balcony seating overlooking Ball Circle.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Linden Terrace as having an outdoor balcony with rocking chairs plus indoor soft furniture and tables and chairs; it is open for seating when not booked.
cards.source_title: About the Cedric Rucker University Center | University of Mary Washington
cards.access_notes: Open for seating when not booked for an event; CRUC academic-year building hours are daily 7 a.m.–10 p.m.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public-facing destinations on the downtown corridors reached from UMW via College Avenue and William Street.

cards.entity_name: Fredericksburg Branch, Central Rappahannock Regional Library
cards.title: Fredericksburg Branch: an evening library stop
cards.subtitle: Caroline Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the public branch at 1201 Caroline Street for a focused reading or research stop; verify holiday closures before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A downtown public library with weekday evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fredericksburg Branch is at 1201 Caroline Street and lists Monday through Thursday hours of 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.
cards.source_title: Fredericksburg Branch | Central Rappahannock Regional Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m.; Friday–Saturday close at 5:30 p.m.; closed Sunday. Check closures before visiting.

cards.title: Fredericksburg Area Museum: local-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: Princess Anne Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Town Hall/Market House museum at 907 Princess Anne Street and choose an exhibition or program that fits your available time.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission museum in the historic Town Hall/Market House.
cards.evidence_claim: Fredericksburg Area Museum is at 907 Princess Anne Street, offers free admission, and presents regional-history exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists 10 a.m.–5 p.m. hours and says it is closed Monday; confirm before a visit.

cards.title: Visitor Center: orient yourself downtown
cards.subtitle: Caroline Street corridor
cards.notes: Start at 601 Caroline Street to pick up downtown information, then select one nearby gallery, historic site, or walking route.
cards.short_summary: A city visitor resource in the historic district.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fredericksburg Visitor Center is at 601 Caroline Street in the city’s 40-block National Historic District.
cards.access_notes: The city lists daily hours of 9 a.m.–4 p.m., with First Friday hours extending to 8 p.m.

cards.title: Hurkamp Park: fountain and market setting
cards.subtitle: William Street and Prince Edward Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause by the fountain or use the bike repair station at this downtown park; check the city calendar if you want to pair it with the market.
cards.short_summary: A public park with fountain, seating, and a year-round farmers market.
cards.evidence_claim: Hurkamp Park at 500 William Street has a fountain, benches, bike repair station, restrooms, and hosts the year-round Fredericksburg Farmers Market.
cards.access_notes: The city states the park is open daily from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; rentals may affect organized use.

cards.title: James Monroe Museum: presidential artifacts
cards.subtitle: Charles Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan a museum visit at 908 Charles Street and use its interpretation to connect Fredericksburg with the fifth president’s legacy.
cards.short_summary: A downtown museum holding Monroe-related artifacts and documents.
cards.evidence_claim: The James Monroe Museum at 908 Charles Street holds the country’s largest collection of artifacts and documents related to James Monroe.
cards.source_title: James Monroe Museum and Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s visit information for current admissions and opening details.

cards.title: Mary Washington House: an 18th-century home
cards.subtitle: Charles Street corridor
cards.notes: Add the house at 1200 Charles Street to a downtown history walk, and consult the operator for current tour availability before arrival.
cards.short_summary: The last Fredericksburg home of Mary Ball Washington.
cards.evidence_claim: Mary Ball Washington spent the final 17 years of her life at the Mary Washington House, 1200 Charles Street.
cards.source_title: Washington Heritage Museums | Event Space Rental
cards.access_notes: This is a historic-house museum site; contact Washington Heritage Museums for current public tour access.

cards.title: Rising Sun Tavern: early Fredericksburg history
cards.subtitle: Caroline Street corridor
cards.notes: See the historic building at 1304 Caroline Street as part of a daytime history walk; confirm public museum access with its operator.
cards.short_summary: A former tavern building operated as a historic site.
cards.evidence_claim: Rising Sun Tavern at 1304 Caroline Street was built by Charles Washington around 1760 and later operated as a tavern.
cards.source_title: Washington Heritage Museums | Event Space Rental
cards.access_notes: Visit for historic interpretation only; check Washington Heritage Museums for public tour access.

cards.title: Hugh Mercer Apothecary: historic medical practice
cards.subtitle: Caroline Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the restored shop at 1020 Caroline Street to examine how an eighteenth-century Fredericksburg medical practice was interpreted.
cards.short_summary: A restored apothecary associated with Dr. Hugh Mercer.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hugh Mercer Apothecary at 1020 Caroline Street interprets Dr. Mercer’s Fredericksburg medical practice and period remedies.
cards.access_notes: The source lists seasonal daily hours; confirm current museum operations before visiting.

cards.title: Kenmore: Washington Avenue historic house
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Include the historic house at 1201 Washington Avenue on a daytime walk and check its official visitor information for scheduled tours.
cards.short_summary: A named historic-house destination on Washington Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenmore is located at 1201 Washington Avenue in Fredericksburg.
cards.source_title: Historic Garden Week 2025 Retail Outlets with Guidebooks
cards.access_notes: Confirm current public hours and admissions directly with Kenmore before traveling there.

cards.title: Sunken Road: self-guided battlefield walk
cards.subtitle: Sunken Road corridor off Lafayette Boulevard
cards.notes: Follow the NPS walking route from the Fredericksburg Battlefield area to see the road, Marye’s Heights, and National Cemetery context.
cards.short_summary: A half-mile NPS interpretive route through a battlefield landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS describes the Sunken Road Walking Trail as a 0.5-mile route along Sunken Road and up Marye’s Heights to Fredericksburg National Cemetery.
cards.source_title: Visitor Centers | Fredericksburg & Spotsylvania National Military Park
cards.access_notes: Park grounds are generally open sunrise to sunset; check NPS alerts and current operating hours before visiting.

warnings: Coordinates and Google Maps links are omitted because they were not independently verified from a primary map source.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten university-documented UMW traditions that mark the academic year from new-student arrival through commencement.

cards.title: Pledge the Honor Code
cards.subtitle: University of Mary Washington
cards.notes: Attend the academic-regalia ceremony and listen for the community pledge to uphold the Honor Code in every interaction.
cards.short_summary: A formal campus pledge centered on UMW’s Honor Code.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies Honor Convocation as a tradition where students pledge to uphold the Honor Code and faculty attend in academic regalia.
cards.access_notes: University ceremony; consult the current student-events calendar for attendance details.

cards.title: Light a Candle on Ball Circle
cards.subtitle: August • Ball Circle
cards.notes: Join the new-year gathering on Ball Circle, where students light candles and begin their journey as UMW Eagles.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit welcome marking the start of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Eagle Gathering as an August tradition in which students convene on Ball Circle and light a candle.
cards.access_notes: New-academic-year program; confirm the current schedule and participation details with UMW.

cards.title: Bring the Family to Campus
cards.subtitle: September or October
cards.notes: Plan around the annual family visit weekend, with campus time, food, and entertainment intended for students and their families.
cards.short_summary: A fall campus weekend for students and visiting families.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW lists Family Weekend as a September/October tradition where families join students on campus for food and entertainment.
cards.access_notes: Dates and individual event access vary by year; check UMW’s current Family Weekend information.

cards.title: Build Up to Homecoming
cards.subtitle: October
cards.notes: Follow the October run-up to Homecoming for campus games, lip sync, food, prizes, and varsity athletic contests.
cards.short_summary: A week of Eagle-pride events leading into Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says Spirit Week precedes Homecoming and includes activities, games, lip sync, food, prizes, and varsity contests.
cards.access_notes: October programming varies annually; review the official events calendar for the current lineup.

cards.title: Count Down 100 Days
cards.subtitle: February • Senior tradition
cards.notes: If you are a senior, mark the 100-day countdown to graduation at this casino-themed class celebration.
cards.short_summary: A senior milestone held 100 days before graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies 100th Night as a February casino-themed event for seniors marking 100 days until graduation.
cards.access_notes: Senior-focused event; verify the current event details and eligibility with UMW.

cards.title: Celebrate the Junior Ring
cards.subtitle: March
cards.notes: Watch for Ring Week announcements, including the Junior Ring Dance and ring-presentation ceremony recognizing eligible juniors.
cards.short_summary: A March rite recognizing juniors eligible to wear a class ring.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Junior Ring Week as a cherished tradition with a Junior Ring Dance and a ceremony presenting rings to eligible juniors.
cards.access_notes: Ring purchase and event participation details should be confirmed with the current Junior Class Council information.

cards.title: Wait for the Secret Reveal
cards.subtitle: April
cards.notes: Follow Class Council’s formal announcement for the previously secret location, then plan ahead if tickets are required.
cards.short_summary: A Class Council-planned formal with a location revealed close to the event.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Spring Formal as a secret-planned Class Council event with an undisclosed location, tickets, dinner, and dancing.
cards.access_notes: UMW states tickets generally sell out; check the current announcement before making plans.

cards.title: Pick Devils or Goats
cards.subtitle: April • Ball Circle
cards.notes: Join the spring carnival and class competitions: even-year graduates are Goats, while odd-year graduates are Devils.
cards.short_summary: UMW’s long-running friendly competition between odd- and even-year graduating classes.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW calls Devil-Goat Day one of its oldest traditions and documents the Devil/Goat graduation-year teams and Ball Circle competition.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally held the Thursday before the last spring day of classes; verify the current location and schedule.

cards.title: Recognize Campus Service
cards.subtitle: April
cards.notes: Attend the recognition ceremony honoring students, organizations, staff, and faculty for leadership and service through campus involvement.
cards.short_summary: An April ceremony celebrating leadership, service, and graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says the Eagle Awards Ceremony recognizes leadership and service by students, organizations, staff, and faculty, and includes senior recognition.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony details and nomination or attendance information vary by year.

cards.title: Close Out Senior Year
cards.subtitle: May • Anderson Center
cards.notes: For graduating seniors, watch for the Thursday-night gathering before commencement, with formal dress, food, music, and reminiscing.
cards.short_summary: A formal senior capstone held just before commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Grad Ball as a tradition generally held in the Anderson Center on the Thursday before Saturday commencement.
cards.access_notes: Senior-focused program; check current commencement-week communications for admission and schedule details.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Mary Washington, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for learning the Fredericksburg campus and making one nearby Saturday stop.

cards.title: Start with a Campus Walk lap
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • main Fredericksburg campus
cards.notes: Walk the brick spine from one end of campus to the other, using the benches and gathering areas to orient yourself before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A practical first pass through UMW’s central pedestrian route.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes Campus Walk as a large brick walkway through the center of campus with benches and gathering places.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; use normal campus-safety awareness.

cards.title: Find Jefferson Square at the front gates
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • beside Double Drive
cards.notes: Use this named square by the main gates as a reference point, then trace the commencement route toward the Bell Tower to learn the campus layout.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable starting landmark at UMW’s College Avenue entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies Jefferson Square as adjacent to Double Drive and the main gates of the Fredericksburg Campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark adjacent to the main gates.

cards.title: Pause at the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • between Jefferson Square and Campus Walk
cards.notes: Continue from Jefferson Square through the Bell Tower and take a photo for your own campus-reference album before moving down Campus Walk.
cards.short_summary: A named landmark on UMW’s ceremonial campus route.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW’s commencement route runs from Jefferson Square through the Bell Tower and down Campus Walk.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; keep clear when university events require the route.

cards.title: End the first walk at Ball Circle
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Campus Walk terminus
cards.notes: Make Ball Circle your turnaround point, then decide whether to head to a campus building or meet classmates back along the pedestrian route.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark that anchors the end of the walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW identifies Ball Circle as a campus landmark and places it at the end of the commencement procession from Campus Walk.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow posted directions during events.

cards.title: Regroup at the CRUC
cards.subtitle: Friday early evening • 7:00 AM–10:00 PM during the academic year
cards.notes: Use the lounge, student-facing offices, and dining areas to make a simple evening plan; check the dining site before relying on a specific outlet.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building for dining, study, student services, and scheduled events.
cards.evidence_claim: The CRUC includes dining, study and social spaces, student offices, and academic-year building hours of 7 AM–10 PM daily.
cards.source_title: About the Cedric Rucker University Center
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are 7:00 AM–10:00 PM daily; dining may have different or limited break hours.

cards.title: Choose a Simpson Library study perch
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Fredericksburg campus
cards.notes: Locate the study rooms, sunrooms, and third-floor treehouses so you have a calm, practical place ready for your first reading or group project.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with individual and group study settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson Library has study areas on all three floors, group tables, reservable study rooms, sunrooms, and third-floor treehouse carrels.
cards.access_notes: Library service and building hours vary by term; consult the library before a late visit.

cards.title: Cross into the Hurley Convergence Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • connected to Simpson Library
cards.notes: Walk the library bridge into the HCC and note its information desk, gallery, and technology-oriented spaces for future class projects.
cards.short_summary: An academic commons directly connected to Simpson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW describes the Hurley Convergence Center as an academic commons and notes its connection to Simpson Library by bridge.
cards.source_title: Research and Cultural Facilities at UMW
cards.access_notes: Use building services according to posted access and reservation rules.

cards.title: Take a daylight fitness-center orientation
cards.subtitle: Saturday daytime • end of Campus Walk
cards.notes: Bring your EagleOne ID, ask the front desk about access, and take a short equipment-orientation lap rather than committing to a full workout on day one.
cards.short_summary: A student-access recreation facility attached to Goolrick Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW states that its recreational spaces are in and around Goolrick Hall and that enrolled students access facilities with an EagleOne ID.
cards.access_notes: Enrolled students present EagleOne ID at the front desk; facility schedules and closures change by term.

cards.title: Check out the University Tennis Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • UMW athletic facility
cards.notes: If tennis or pickleball interests you, review the center’s current booking information and ask about student open-play options before bringing a racquet.
cards.short_summary: An 18-court UMW tennis complex that supports student classes, club tennis, and open play.
cards.evidence_claim: UMW says the University Tennis Center has 18 courts and that students may use it through PE classes, Club Tennis, and open play activities.
cards.access_notes: Current students may reserve tennis play free with valid UMW ID; confirm hours and availability before going.

cards.entity_name: Fredericksburg Farmers Market at Hurkamp Park
cards.title: Make a Saturday market loop at Hurkamp Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • 500 William Street, Fredericksburg
cards.notes: Browse the open-air market, then use the walk as a gentle introduction to downtown; purchases are optional and vendor offerings change seasonally.
cards.short_summary: A current Saturday market option in downtown Fredericksburg.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists the main Fredericksburg Farmers Market season at Hurkamp Park on Saturdays, 7 AM–1 PM, through December 5, 2026.
cards.access_notes: Main market season is Saturdays 7:00 AM–1:00 PM at 500 William Street through December 5, 2026; offerings are sold by vendors.
